_note: Checked-in map for lint/rule_audit.py. Each key is a `<!-- rule:<slug> -->` anchor in a file that lint/rule_audit.py RULE_FILES names. `mechanism.kind` is one of guard, gate, ci, unmechanized. guard.ref must name a rule string passed to refuse()/record() in hooks/guard.py. gate.ref must be a file path, relative to the repo root, that exists; a gate row cites `test` (path::name, resolved by AST) and/or `setting` (a JSON value in settings.json), never a `needle`. ci.ref must name a `- name:` step in .github/workflows/gates.yml. unmechanized.reason must say what a hook or check would have to see.

mechanism.reason: Judging the outcome for the person served is a human read of context and consequence. No test scores outcome quality.
A stance for how to read a recorded decision, not an independently checkable action a hook can observe.
Naming a stale decision, measuring its claim, and proposing a fix are judgment calls in prose. Nothing parses staleness or fix quality.
Whether a stated act matches the literal word given, versus a variant of it, is a judgment call on wording. No hook parses an instruction and an action for a match.
Whether an argument has rotted is a judgment call on its merit. No test reads argument quality.
Nothing in the repo distinguishes a solo repeal of a decision from one the owner approved.
No hook reads the owner's request and judges whether solo or orchestrate fits it, or checks that the session said its pick in one line first.
Nothing counts the edits in a request or sees whether parts could run in parallel, so no check can tell a solo job from an orchestrate job.
No check classifies a diff as touching a rule's behaviour, a gate's verdict, or program logic versus text, style, and content, so none can demand the reviewer.
Nothing watches a solo job's edit count or parallel parts over time, or sees whether the session said its switch in one line.

No hook classifies a session's own act as orchestration versus building, or judges whether a change can move a verdict. hooks/decision_watch.py, a Stop command hook, reads the transcript and this turn's git diff and judges the act, escalating to a model only for the residual judgment a diff cannot make, which is this rule's check.
Nothing inspects which role, builder, reviewer, or Explore, a spawned agent holds at runtime, or catches a worker that carries two.
The owner ruled on 2026-09-28 that prose alone enforces the ceiling and that no forcing returns, so no hook or setting blocks a model above Sonnet.
Judging whether a task is Opus-shaped, and whether the assistant said so in one line first, is a human read of the transcript.
No check parses a brief for the task, files, governing rulings, and a done-check. Brief quality is read by a human.
Nothing distinguishes a resumed agent from a freshly spawned one at the tool layer this repo governs.
No check counts checkouts against concurrent workers or catches two agents sharing one tree.
Nothing inspects the isolation field a workflow agent invocation carries.
Lane assignment and briefing happen in chat and briefs, which no hook here reads.
No hook reads inter-lane messages for content or timing to catch a mid-task exchange.
Naming the open lanes correctly is a factual claim written in prose, not a structure a check can verify.
No check counts how many agents hold a given checkout at once.
guard.py acts on the command itself. Nothing checks that the assistant confirmed its checkout and branch before issuing it.
No check compares the ports or data paths two checkouts use.
Detecting an incident and confirming a re-verify followed it both need a human read of the transcript.
Branch protection on main is a GitHub repository setting, external to this codebase. No file here proves it is switched on.
Waiting is a behavior in time. No artifact records whether the assistant waited before it acted again.
Enforcement is GitHub's required-status-checks setting on the branch, not something this repo's files can attest to.

mechanism.test: actions/stamp/test_stamp.mjs::frontmatter --check refuses a new record numbered on a feature branch

mechanism.reason: No lint checks citation style in a commit message or a PR body for an id versus a bare path.
No check enforces one file per decision or a separate folder per record kind.
Whether a new entry restates an open question or opens a new one is a judgment about meaning. A hook sees a new file, not its question.
Sequencing overlapping PRs into one integration branch and closing the originals is a manual coordination step.
No harness renders every screen at every size and theme and demands a verdict line per screen.
Whether a headless or isolated browser would have done, and whether a login was needed for a given check, are judgment calls, not a loggable fact this repo captures.
No hook sees a browser launch, a screencapture call, or computer use before it happens and checks a one-line announcement preceded it.
No check reads whether a report about long work was verified against the repo instead of a status line. The mutation harness's WRONG CAUSE verdict covers only mutant cause of death, not this.
No check reads whether a block-list was tested by running it for real. The guard suite drives the guard as a subprocess, but nothing proves a dry run would be refused.
No check compares a dependency bump's target version against the first version that fixed the named problem.
lint/ste_lint.py checks sentence style, not whether a published number or path has a reader that actually checked it.
No check measures how much of a document a session read before acting on it.
No check tells a pasted verdict apart from a pasted stream, or counts the commands used to get it.
Nothing inspects a brief's content to confirm it names files rather than pasting their contents.
No check tells whether the orchestrator read a sub-agent's report or its full transcript.
Compaction content is a judgment call about what to keep. Nothing scores a compacted context against this rule.
Telling a guessed answer from a computed one needs a read of the reasoning, which no check performs.
Whether an ambiguity was surfaced or silently resolved is a judgment call on the reply's content.
No check compares a task's item list against a reply to catch a silently dropped item.
A hook would have to see two implementations of one capability in the repo.
Distinguishing a cause fix from a symptom fix is a code-review judgment, not a parseable property.
Whether a fix is a bandaid, and whether it was named as one, is a judgment call on the report text.
Nothing checks that a design discussed in chat was later landed in a spec, a decision entry, or declared abandoned.
No lint checks that a decision citation in a reply carries an id plus a short gloss rather than a bare id.
Judging whether a rule explanation ran to a paragraph is a style read, not a parsed structure.

No hook diffs an edit to a record and judges whether superseded text was rewritten in place versus left beside a story, an old quote, or the owner's verbatim words. Judging what is still true is a human read.
No check reads whether the first sentence of a reply is the point rather than a preamble.
Whether a turn only tracked running work, and whether the reply held to one line, is a content judgment.
No check compares a reply against a worker's report to catch an echoed copy or a described screenshot.
No check tells a pasted command stream apart from a stated verdict in a reply.
Whether a decision was framed as a question with options and a recommendation is a style read of the reply.
lint/report_gate.py checks the label headers only. It does not read whether Done's line says BUILT, RECORDED, or OTHER, or names a PR or commit.
No check counts whether a label held one inline item or several as bullets.
The report gate accepts any in-order subset of the four labels, so it cannot see whether a label that stays in the report is empty or does not apply.
No check reads a green result and reports which platforms and fixture states it did not cover. The CI matrix runs three platforms, which is coverage, not a check on how a reader treats the green.

Nothing checks that an answer given in chat reached a decision entry or a deferred item before the work it governs merged. A check would have to pair each AskUserQuestion answer with a tracked path that a later report names.
No check tells narration or a recap of earlier work apart from new content in a reply.
Whether a question was simple, and whether the answer held to 1 to 3 sentences, is a content judgment.
No check reads whether the user asked for full detail and whether the reply then gave it.
No check finds an error report, failing output, security warning, or destructive confirmation and measures whether it was cut.
Whether a reply dropped a true and needed fact to stay short is a judgment no check can make.
No check holds a list of jargon, and plain words depend on what the reader already knows.
No check finds a technical term in a reply and reads whether an everyday gloss sits beside it.
No check finds a question to the user and reads whether one plain sentence before it states the problem and why it needs their word.
Whether a step handed to the user was doable is a judgment on the reply and the tools available. No check reads a reply and the tool list to decide that.
No check reads whether each option in a question says what the user gains and what the user loses.
No check sees the text of a reply beside its question box and reads whether the question depends on text outside the box.
